issues.legal_issue: Compensation for comparable acquired land should be adjusted to reflect changes in market value between the earlier benchmark acquisition and later acquisitions.
material_facts: The appeals concerned land acquired on four different dates after comparable land in the same village had been acquired in 1974.
In an earlier decision concerning the comparable land, the Court had fixed compensation at Rs. 17.50 per square yard after considering the relevant facts and lower court judgments.
The Court considered that market prices had risen between 1974 and 1978 and fixed compensation rates of Rs. 20, Rs. 25, Rs. 26 and Rs. 30 per square yard for the respective acquisition dates.
issues.conclusion: The market value was directed to be calculated at the rates fixed for each acquisition date: Rs. 20, Rs. 25, Rs. 26 and Rs. 30 per square yard, respectively.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on its earlier decision in Paltoo Singh v. State of Haryana, which fixed the value of comparable land acquired in 1974 at Rs. 17.50 per square yard. Having regard to the rise in market prices through 1978, it considered it fair and reasonable to adjust the compensation for the different acquisition dates. The relevant acquisition dates were those stated in the Section 4 notifications.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and prior_comparable_land_award and later_acquisition_dates and intervening_market_price_rise

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.prior_comparable_land_award: A court has fixed compensation for comparable land acquired earlier.
predicates.later_acquisition_dates: The land in the proceeding was acquired after the comparable land.
predicates.intervening_market_price_rise: Market prices rose between the earlier comparable acquisition and the later acquisitions.
predicates.compensation_adjusted_for_acquisition_ti: Compensation is adjusted to reflect the difference in acquisition timing.

issues.definition: When a land acquisition compensation appeal concerns later-acquired land, a prior award for comparable land, and an intervening rise in market prices, compensation is adjusted to reflect acquisition timing.

issues.legal_issue: A claim valuation may be amended on an oral request despite an unpaid court-fee shortfall, but enhanced compensation is payable only after the required court fee is paid.
material_facts: In some compensation appeals, the court fee paid did not cover the full amount of compensation awarded.
No formal amendment application had been filed, but an oral request to amend the claim valuation was made.
The Court permitted the amendment and made payment of the enhanced compensation conditional on payment of court fee in accordance with law.
issues.conclusion: The oral request to amend the claim valuation was allowed, and enhanced compensation was payable upon payment of the required court fee.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its procedural discretion to permit amendment of the claim valuation on an oral request, notwithstanding the absence of a formal amendment petition, while requiring court fee to be paid in accordance with law before enhanced compensation was paid. No earlier case was cited for this direction.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.court_fee_shortfall: The court fee paid does not cover the full compensation claimed or awarded.
predicates.oral_claim_amendment_request: A party orally asks to amend the claim valuation without filing a formal amendment application.
predicates.claim_amendment_permitted_subject_to_req: The claim amendment is permitted, but enhanced compensation is payable only after the required court fee is paid.

issues.definition: In a land acquisition compensation appeal, an oral request to amend a claim despite a court-fee shortfall may be allowed, with enhanced compensation dependent on payment of the required fee.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in applications to substitute legal representatives may be condoned, while disputes about representative status or entitlement to compensation may be determined by the land acquisition authorities.
material_facts: Some appellants had died while the appeals were pending.
Applications to bring their legal representatives on record were filed late.
The Court allowed the applications and stated that disputes about legal-representative status or compensation claims could be raised before the land acquisition authorities.
issues.conclusion: The delay was condoned and the substitution applications were allowed, with any dispute about legal representatives or compensation claims left to be raised before the land acquisition authorities.
issues.legal_principle: The Court condoned the delay and allowed substitution applications in the appeals, while reserving disputes about legal representation or compensation entitlement for the land acquisition authorities. No earlier case or specific statutory provision was cited for this direction.

predicates.pending_appeal: An appeal remains pending when a party dies.
predicates.deceased_appellant: An appellant dies while the appeal is pending.
predicates.delayed_substitution_application: An application to bring the deceased appellant's legal representatives on record is filed late.
predicates.substitution_allowed_after_delay_condone: Delay is condoned and substitution is allowed, while disputes about representation or compensation entitlement are left to the relevant authorities.

issues.definition: When an appellant dies during a pending appeal and a substitution application is late, delay may be condoned and substitution allowed, with representation or compensation disputes left to the relevant authorities.
